question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: KEPT = the elements of findings that are maps, in list order; every other element (none, text, number, bool, list) is skipped and leaves no line and no separator. The result is the rendered line of each element of KEPT, in order, joined by a single LF (U+000A); no LF before the first line or after the last. An empty KEPT (the empty list, or a list of skipped elements only) yields the empty text; one kept element yields its line with no LF at all. CITED FIDELITY package — the fix of 9e2245be5f42: one bad element never aborts the output
FIELD(e, k) for a kept element e is the value e holds under key k, or ABSENT when e has no key k. ABSENT and none read alike everywhere below.

Each line is, in exactly this order with no other separator or whitespace: "::", LEVEL, " file=", PROP(TEXT-OF(path)), then LINE-PART, then ",title=", PROP(TEXT-OF(title)), "::", DATA(TEXT-OF(message)). path, title and message are FIELD(e, "path"), FIELD(e, "title"), FIELD(e, "message"). The file property and the title property are always written, with an empty value when their field is ABSENT or none.

LEVEL is FIELD(e, "level") when that is exactly the text error, warning or notice (case-sensitive, no trimming); anything else (another text, a non-text value, ABSENT) gives the text "error", so an unknown level fails toward the most visible annotation. LEVEL is never escaped. CITED FIDELITY package — kept by ruling (F8)

LINE-PART: let L = FIELD(e, "line"). When L is a number with no fractional part and 1 <= L <= 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1, the largest SAFE integer), LINE-PART is ",line=" followed by L as plain decimal digits (no sign, no point, no exponent). Otherwise LINE-PART is empty: ABSENT, none, text (also "3"), bool, list, map, NaN, an infinity, zero, negative zero, a negative number, a fraction, and every number from 2^53 up (9007199254740992, 1e21) all omit it. CITED FIDELITY package — the fix of 9e2245be5f42 (F2): only a safe positive integer is written
TEXT-OF(v), the text a field value renders as, by TABLE TEXT-OF. Coercion applies before escaping.
ABSENT or none                        | the empty text (never "undefined" or "null")
bool                                  | "true" or "false"
text                                  | itself, unchanged
number                                | NUM-TEXT(v) (R7)

list                                  | the TEXT-OF of each element joined by "," with no spaces; an element that is none renders as the empty text; a nested list renders by the same rule (so [[1,[2]],3] gives 1,2,3); the empty list gives the empty text
map without an own key toString       | the text "[object Object]" (its entries never matter; a key valueOf alone does not change this)

map with an own key toString          | throws, for the whole call (whatever that key holds, none included), whether at the top or nested inside a list at any depth CITED FIDELITY package — kept by ruling (F4): the host's text conversion finds a toString member that is not callable, and the map's other members yield no primitive; only text reaches this code from the review

NUM-TEXT(x) is the shortest round-trip decimal text of the double x in the ECMAScript Number-to-String form: NaN gives "NaN"; the infinities give "Infinity" and "-Infinity"; both zeros give "0" (no sign); otherwise a leading - for a negative, then, with k significant digits s and decimal exponent n (value = s * 10^(n-k), s the shortest digit string that reads back as x): plain digits with no point when k <= n <= 21 (trailing zeros padded: 1e20 gives 100000000000000000000); a point after the first n digits when 0 < n < k; "0." then -n zeros then the digits when -6 < n <= 0 (0.000001); otherwise exponent form: the first digit, then "." and the rest when k > 1, then "e", then "+" or "-", then the decimal |n-1| (1e+21, 1e-7, 1.7976931348623157e+308). There is never a trailing ".0" and never a leading "+" on the mantissa.

PROP(t), the property escape for path and title, replaces in t, character by character, using TABLE ESCAPES column PROP; DATA(t), the data escape for message, uses column DATA. Every other character, including U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, TAB, VT, FF, "=", "::"-forming colons in DATA and every non-ASCII character, passes unchanged. The replacement is one pass over the original characters: an inserted "%" is never escaped again, so "%0A" in the input becomes "%250A" and a real LF becomes "%0A". CITED FIDELITY package — the code runs the replacements in sequence with "%" first, which is equivalent
: (U+003A)  | %3A | unchanged
, (U+002C)  | %2C | unchanged
